title: Cold rebuild: A session store
summary: Rebuild A session store from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **A session store** in *Server-side sessions*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: What does this print? (The random bytes differ every run; the lengths do not.)
steps.explain: Hex uses 2 characters per byte. Base64 uses 4 characters for every 3 bytes, rounded up with padding: 32 bytes need 44 characters. 16 bytes are 128 bits.

steps.title: Rebuild A session store cold
prompt: Write a class `SessionStore` that keeps sessions in memory.
- `string Create(string user, DateTimeOffset now)`: makes a new 256-bit random id (as 64 hex characters), stores the session, returns the id.

- `string? GetUser(string id, DateTimeOffset now)`: returns the user, or `null` when the id is unknown or the session has expired (idle **or** absolute, using `>=`). An expired session is removed. A successful lookup moves the idle clock forward to `now`.
The tests already import `System.Security.Cryptography`; don't add `using` lines.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
public string Create(string user, DateTimeOffset now) => "";
public string? GetUser(string id, DateTimeOffset now) => null;
